title: GPT-6 Astra Drives Proof That the Core Always Exists in Approval-Based Committee Elections
whyItMatters: Resolves the central 2017 open problem in approval-based multiwinner voting—and marks the first "Major Advance" solved on Epoch AI’s FrontierMath: Open Problems—via a harmonic-entropy objective found with GPT-6 Astra.
summary: Patrick Becker, Matthias Greger, and Dominik Peters resolved the central open problem of approval-based committee elections posed by Aziz et al. (2017): proving that a core-stable committee always exists and can be computed in polynomial time. By strengthening the core to fractional-deviation core+, applying LP duality to obtain payment certificates, and maximizing a novel harmonic-entropy objective whose key idea emerged from an interactive research session with GPT-6 Astra, the result became the first solved problem in the "Major Advance" tier of Epoch AI’s FrontierMath: Open Problems.
technicalHighlights: Resolves the 2017 Aziz–Brill–Conitzer–Elkind–Freeman–Walsh open question by proving the core is always non-empty and polynomial-time computable.
First "Major Advance"-tier problem solved on Epoch AI’s FrontierMath: Open Problems benchmark board.
Uses a novel harmonic-entropy payment objective discovered in a sustained interactive session with GPT-6 Astra, explicitly credited by the authors and Epoch AI.
caveats: Currently an arXiv preprint (arXiv:2609.11912v2, revised Nov 3, 2026) without Lean formalization; Epoch AI classifies it as a human+AI collaboration rather than a bare-prompt autonomous solve.

scoreRationale.foundational: Settles the defining existence and tractability conjecture of proportional multiwinner voting theory.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly impacts participatory budgeting, collective decision-making mechanisms, and AI-assisted theoretical economics.
scoreRationale.verification: 43-page rewritten preprint by the field’s leading researchers (including the problem’s benchmark proposer), undergoing peer review.
scoreRationale.velocity: Delivered the decisive harmonic-entropy potential function after 9 years of partial approximations.
